latin.475: §. XI. (7.) Sensui emunitiori nec uni tantum, sed pluribus: Enimvero panem & vinum in S. Eucharistia non annihilari, nec in horum locum, corpus & sanguinem Christi, corporaliter substitui, tàm visus & tactus, quàm gustus & olfactus, distinctè evincunt; Quorum distinctum testimonium præsertim ab omnibus unà perhibitum, in dubium vocandum haud esse.
latin.476: Ipsa revelata Scriptura S. non unô modô edicit (1) Semet ipsam sensibus nostris, i. e. Lectioni & Auditioni commendando, id quod temere faceret, si sensibus fides habenda non sit. (2) Imperium in Sensus Rationi, præsertim illuminatæ, deferendo certisque limitibus circumscrivendo, in quod frustra niteretur, si Sensuum actus fallibiles sint.
latin.477: (3) Ad Sensuum testimonium, in Veritate à se confirmanda stabiliendaque, provocando, tùm per Christum ipsum: Vide manus meas & pedes meos, nam ego ipse sum, Contrectate me & videte, nam Spiritus Carnem & OSSA non habet, sicut me conspicitis habere Luc. 24. 39. tùm per dilectissimum Christi Apostolum: Quod erat à principio &c. 1. Joh. 1, 1. Quod si verò vel uni Sensui benè constituto, nec requisito ullo ad sentiendum destituto, fides meritò habenda, quantò magis pluribus: Cùm, quò plures species, inter se conspirantes, variis modis excitantur, eò perceptio, quæ est earum contemplatio, certior sit. Unde omnium hominum usu frequentatum, ut pluribus Sensibus magis credant, quàm uni atque alteri.
latin.478: Denique (8.) Sui ipsius Nomenclaturæ, quâ Transsubstantiatio dici cupit i. e. Conversio Substantiæ in substantiam, qualis tamen Conversio neutiquam obtinet, suppositô, ex pane & vino per eandem nihil remanere, ut rectius eô nomine Annihilatio substantiæ unius, & alterius substantiæ Creatio, quam Transsubstantiatio, dici mereatur.
latin.479: Scilicet, si istos audiamus, quibus solis datum est hæc βάθη callere (sunt verba Matthæi Wreni in Increpatione Bar Jesu, seu Refutatione Catechismi Racoviensis p. m. 342.) Substantia Panis neutiquam transiit in Substantiam corporis, sed exterrit a (ut par est,) ad Divina illa vocabula, Hoc est corpus meum, tam subito, prorsusque evanuit, ut nè durare quidem tantisper ausa fuerit, dum & Accidentia sua convasare, Speciesque misellas secum auferre posset. Quanto minus opinandum est, Substantiam Divini Corporis transiisse in eam, quæ evanuit, Panis Substantiam?
latin.480: Cui igitur Substantia, aut unde suum Trans? Qua heic Transsubstantiatio est? Translocatio quidem ista est; Succedere enim volunt Corpus de Cælo in Locum Substantiæ Panis; Et Transfiguratio est; Submittere enim se aiunt Sanctum Corpus Figuræ, quam profugus Panis in Speciebus suis (satis inclementer post se relictis) gesserat. Sed ecquid est aliud? Rogandi igitur sunt Romani Correctores, ut & Augustodunensem istam ἀκυρολογίαν corrigere jam velint, & (si fatalis necessitas sic ferat, Error Errori Errorem ut semper pariat, atque Prodigium Dogmatis & nominis stribiligine æternum insigniatur,) ut ab altera porrò literula orsi, appellari hanc nunc jubeant, pro Transsubstantiatione, Vicesubstantiationem.

pass_a.475: §. XI. (7.) To cleaner Sense, and not to one only but to several: For that bread and wine in the Sacred Eucharist are not annihilated, nor in their place Christ’s body and blood corporally substituted, sight and touch as well as taste and smell distinctly prove; Whose distinct testimony, especially when offered by all together, is by no means to be called into doubt.
pass_a.476: Revealed Holy Scripture itself declares in more than one way (1) by recommending itself to our senses, i.e. to Reading and Hearing — which it would do rashly if faith is not to be had in the senses. (2) by deferring empire over the Senses to Reason, especially illuminated, and circumscribing it with certain limits — on which it would lean in vain if the acts of the Senses are fallible.
pass_a.477: (3) by appealing to the testimony of the Senses in confirming and establishing the Truth from itself, both through Christ Himself: See my hands and my feet, for I myself am; Handle me and see, for a Spirit has not Flesh and BONES as you see me have (Luke 24:39), and through Christ’s most beloved Apostle: That which was from the beginning &c. (1 John 1:1). But if faith is rightly to be had even in one Sense well constituted and destitute of no requisite for sensing, how much more in several: Since the more species conspiring among themselves are excited in various ways, the more certain is perception, which is their contemplation. Whence by the frequent use of all men, they trust more senses more than one or another.
pass_a.478: Finally (8.) by its own Nomenclature, by which it wishes to be called Transsubstantiation i.e. Conversion of Substance into substance — which Conversion nonetheless by no means obtains, it being supposed that through the same nothing remains from bread and wine — so that under that name it rather deserves to be called Annihilation of one substance and Creation of another, than Transsubstantiation.
pass_a.479: Namely if we hear those to whom alone it is given to know these depths (Matthew Wren’s words in the Increpatio Bar Jesu, or Refutation of the Racovian Catechism p. 342): The Substance of Bread by no means passed into the Substance of the body, but terrified (as is fair) at those Divine words This is my body, so suddenly and utterly vanished that it did not even dare last long enough to pack its Accidents and carry the poor Species off with itself. How much less is it to be thought that the Substance of the Divine Body passed into that Bread-Substance which vanished?
pass_a.480: To what Substance then, or whence its Trans? What Transsubstantiation is here? This is indeed a Translocation; for they will have the Body succeed from Heaven into the Place of the Bread’s Substance; And it is a Transfiguration; for they say the Holy Body submits itself to the Figure which the fugitive Bread had borne in its Species (left behind itself rather unkindly). But what else is it? Therefore the Roman Correctors are to be asked that they now be willing to correct even that Autun ἀκυρολογία, and (if fatal necessity so bears that Error always beget Error to Error, and the Prodigy of Dogma and name be forever marked with a stribiligo) that starting from another little letter they now order this to be called, instead of Transsubstantiation, Vicesubstantiation.

475: §.XI (7): cleaner Sense — not one only but several.

Sight, touch, taste, and smell distinctly prove bread and wine are not annihilated in the Eucharist, nor Christ’s body and blood corporally put in their place; their joint distinct testimony is not to be doubted.
476: Revealed Scripture itself backs that: (1) it trusts itself to our senses in reading and hearing — rash if senses deserve no faith.
(2) it gives Reason empire over the senses within limits — pointless if sense-acts are fallible.
477: (3) Christ and John appeal to sense to confirm truth: Luke 24:39 (handle me; a spirit has not flesh and bones); 1 John 1:1 (that which was from the beginning).
If one well-constituted sense deserves faith, how much more several conspiring species — all men trust many senses more than one.
478: (8) By its own name: it wants ‘Transsubstantiation’ = conversion of substance into substance.
But if nothing of bread and wine remains, the truer name is annihilation of one substance and creation of another — not Transsubstantiation.
479: Wren (Increpatio Bar Jesu / Racovian Catechism refutation p. 342), on those who alone know these ‘depths’: bread-substance did not pass into body-substance.

Terrified at ‘This is my body,’ it vanished so fast it dared not even pack its accidents and drag the poor species along — still less did divine-body substance pass into that vanished bread-substance.
480: So where is the Trans? This is translocation (body from heaven into bread’s place) and transfiguration (holy body under the fugitive bread’s leftover figure) — not Transsubstantiation.
Ask the Roman correctors to fix Autun’s misnomer: if error must breed error, start from another letter and call it Vicesubstantiation.
Stop before Annotatio IV (true Eucharistic sentence through the ages).
